subject: Hosted API discount schedule — stepwise breakpoints proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@velocityai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API discount schedule — initial stepwise proposal

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is a clean starting point for the usage-based discount ladder we discussed for Velocity AI (see redwood-stepwise-vs-weighted-model.xlsx). High level: we propose a stepwise breakpoint ladder (marginal rates per breakpoint) rather than a single weighted/blended effective rate. The attached workbook includes both approaches and a worked example at $1.5M ARR.

Why stepwise: it keeps invoicing and forecasting straightforward for both sides, aligns incentives for higher usage, and maps cleanly to overage calc in our billing system. Weighted/blended can look simpler on paper but often creates surprising effective rates mid-quarter when usage skews unevenly.

Key proposal (starter):
- 0–250M tokens/month: $0.0008 per token
- 250M–1B tokens/month: $0.0006 per token (marginal)
- 1B+ tokens/month: $0.00045 per token (marginal)
- 12-month committed term with quarterly true-ups and 20% overage cap protection for first 2 quarters

I attached a draft master agreement (MA-terms-draft-2026-09-08.pdf) with the commit and overage language that legal asked for.

Can you confirm whether Velocity prefers marginal-step pricing or a single blended effective rate for purchase order purposes? If you want, I can send a one-page example showing monthly cost under both styles for your finance team.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share expected monthly token profile (if comfortable) or high/low estimate
2) We run the workbook and send a short summary with both marginal and blended effective monthly cost
3) Agree on draft MA and PO timeline

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if helpful.

—Jordan

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear starting point and the attachments. A few questions from procurement and finance here:

1) Can you show a numeric example comparing the two approaches for a 12-month profile where usage starts modest (200M tokens/mo) and ramps to 1.2B tokens/mo by month 9? We want to see month-by-month cashflow differences.
2) On the stepwise ladder, are the breakpoints calendar-month based or aggregated across billing cycles (we run some campaigns that spike irregularly)?
3) Overage protection: your note on 20% for the first two quarters — is that refundable credit or just a reduced overage rate? Needs clarification for our procurement team.

Our preference is to keep PO paperwork simple; procurement tends to prefer a single line item with an effective rate. Finance wants visibility into the marginal math. So both views will be necessary.

Can you provide a short paragraph we can pass to legal describing how penalties/credits work in the stepwise model? Otherwise we will ask for a blended effective rate to be shown on the PO but key terms in the MA.

Thanks,
Sarah
VP, Revenue Operations
Velocity AI
sarah@velocityai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API discount schedule — internal calc and recommended language

Jordan / Karthik —

I reviewed Sarah's ask and put together the month-by-month sheets in the attached workbook (tab 'Velocity ramp example'). Notes:
- I modeled the ramp Sarah described (200M -> 1.2B) across 12 months; included both marginal-step monthly invoice amounts and a blended effective monthly rate for each month.
- For their use case the blended effective rate is ~12% lower in months when usage crosses a breakpoint mid-month, which explains procurement's preference for a single line item.
- Breakpoints should be evaluated on a calendar-month billing cycle in our system (easier to implement). If they need aggregation across months we can support a quarterly true-up but it complicates invoicing/modeling.

Suggested legal-friendly paragraph for MA (draft):
"Stepwise pricing: Customer will be billed at marginal unit rates according to the breakpoints defined in Schedule A. Billing is performed per calendar month. If Customer's monthly usage exceeds the committed tier, overage units shall be billed at the marginal overage rate for the next breakpoint. For the first two calendar quarters following the Effective Date, overage charges in any month that are less than or equal to twenty percent (20%) above committed monthly usage shall be credited back to Customer as a billing adjustment applied to the following invoice. Credits are non-refundable cash adjustments applied to invoices only."

If legal wants refunds instead of invoice credits we will escalate, but credits are usually acceptable and simpler.

Let me know if you want me to produce a one-pager for Sarah's procurement with the blended-PO wording plus an appendix showing the marginal math.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Hosted API discount schedule — stepwise breakpoints proposal (examples included)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the questions. Per your request we ran two formatted examples (see attached workbook): one tab shows the marginal-step invoices month-by-month; the other shows the blended effective rate you could place on a PO. Summary bullets below with concrete numbers for your finance team.

Example (12-month ramp, total tokens = ~6.8B across year):
- Stepwise (marginal invoice totals): Annual cost = $962,400 — invoiced monthly as actual usage at marginal rates.
- Blended effective (single PO line): Effective per-token rate across the same usage = $0.0001415 => Annual cost shown on PO = $963,900 (rounded).
- Delta = $1,500 (0.16% of total) in this scenario — small but varies with timing of spikes.

Breakpoints: we bill by calendar month. For spikes that push a month into a higher breakpoint, only the marginal tokens above the breakpoint are billed at the higher-tier rate (i.e., stepwise marginal). Quarter-level true-ups are possible but add reconciliation overhead; we can include a quarterly true-up clause if Velocity prefers smoothing across months.

Overage protection: the language Marissa suggested is what we typically use: a credit applied to the following invoice for overage up to 20% above committed monthly usage, for the first two quarters after the Effective Date. Credits are non-refundable cash adjustments applied to invoices (not cash refunds). I included the exact paragraph in the attached MA draft.

PO recommendation for procurement: we can supply a single-line PO labeled "Hosted API usage — committed tier (effective blended rate)" containing the blended effective monthly rate for ease of PO processing, and attach Schedule A (breakpoints) and Appendix 1 (marginal math) to the MA so finance has visibility. Billing will still occur based on marginal usage; the PO is for purchasing/approval only.

Next steps:
- If that approach works, procurement can issue a PO with the blended effective rate (I can generate the PO numbers once you confirm the target monthly commit).
- If procurement needs us to show a different format, tell me what they need on the PO and we will adapt.

Would you like me to set a 20–30 minute call to run through the spreadsheet with finance/procurement live? Happy to do that this week.

Best,
